question: The HCF and the LCM of two numbers are 17 and 1224, respectively. If one of the numbers is 136, find the other one.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any two numbers, the product of the numbers equals the product of their HCF and LCM.

Second Number = (HCF × LCM) ÷ First Number

Second Number = (17 × 1224) ÷ 136

Second Number = 1224 ÷ 8 = 153

**∴ The correct answer is 153.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

HCF = 17

LCM = 1224

First number (N₁) = 136

**Formula Used:**

N₁ × N₂ = HCF × LCM

 
 Product of Numbers
 136 × N₂
 =
 
 HCF × LCM
 17 × 1224

**Calculations:**

⇒ 136 × N₂ = 17 × 1224

⇒ N₂ = (17 × 1224) ÷ 136

⇒ N₂ = 1224 ÷ 8

⇒ N₂ = 153

**∴ The correct answer is 153.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF and LCM Relation

For any two numbers 'a' and 'b', the product of the numbers is always equal to the product of their HCF and LCM (a × b = HCF × LCM).

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are said to be co-prime if their highest common factor (HCF) is 1. The LCM of two co-prime numbers is simply their product.

Fractions HCF and LCM

HCF of fractions = (HCF of numerators) ÷ (LCM of denominators). LCM of fractions = (LCM of numerators) ÷ (HCF of denominators).
